solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: (&3dn.) Blair (Left ousted by Mandelson primarily) bit stupid to be trapped by Brown? Inane responses here

definitions.note: describes the place where such answers are collected, Private Eye's column

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of the name it follows
one thing being ousted by another means it is thrown out and the other takes its place
something stupid is muddled, so the combined letters come out jumbled
being trapped means being held inside, so the jumble sits within the colour word

blocks.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
the former Labour prime minister's name, taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left; this letter is removed
the first letter of Peter Mandelson, Blair's ally, replaces the L
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jibe that Tony Blair, his left-wing roots ditched under Mandelson's influence, is a bit thick for being caught out by Gordon Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Dumb Britain is a long-running Private Eye column quoting idiotic quiz-show answers. 'Brown' is a colour here, not Gordon Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: The magazine column collects foolish replies given by contestants on television and radio quizzes, so it is literally where such answers live.

clue.text: "Foreskin intact" not edited out?

blocks.note: first meaning: not circumcised
second meaning: a film or text shown in full, with nothing removed

explanation.surface: A smutty question about whether a mention of an intact foreskin survived the censor.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both an uncircumcised penis and a film or book released complete without any editorial removals.

clue.text: see 1ac.
Be the assertive partner taking no time at all to penetrate girlfriend?

indicators.note: penetrating something means getting inside it, so these letters go within the other word

blocks.note: a date is someone you are going out with
O is a zero, nothing
MIN, a minute, is a moment's time; 'at all' completes the phrase 'no time at all'

explanation.surface: A bedroom question about which partner takes charge, rushing straight into a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to control or take charge, the role of the more forceful party in any relationship.

clue.text: Due to defect to Ukip, say?

definitions.note: noun sense: what one is due, as in just deserts

blocks.note: first meaning: a deserved reward or punishment
second meaning: to abandon one's party, as Tory MPs who joined Ukip did

explanation.surface: A politician is about to cross the floor and join Ukip.
explanation.walkthrough: Ukip is the UK Independence Party, which two Conservative MPs joined in 2014. The first meaning survives mainly in the phrase 'just deserts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert, in the old sense, is what someone deserves, while to desert is to walk out on one's side or cause.

clue.text: After Miliband gets started, too much to include first hint of economics, so here's musical item

indicators.note: getting started points to just the opening letter of the leader's name
a first hint is the earliest trace, the initial letter of the word that follows
including something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the first letter of Ed Miliband, then Labour leader
OTT is short for over the top, excessive
the opening letter of economics

explanation.surface: Once Miliband gets going, his excessive talk of economics is set to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts M before the rest: OTT holding E gives OTET.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition, usually sacred and unaccompanied, so it is a piece of music.

clue.text: Paisley's gone heavenward? Examine at end of day for innocence

indicators.note: in a down entry, going heavenward means reading upwards, so the name runs backwards
the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: Ian Paisley, the Northern Irish unionist leader
to vet is to check carefully
the last letter of day

explanation.surface: Ian Paisley has died and gone to heaven, and his record is examined for innocence at day's end.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Paisley died in September 2014, which gives 'gone heavenward' its double edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is a lack of worldly experience, an unsuspecting simplicity close to innocence.

clue.text: Reckless, to do which, toys with Ukip's heart? Ask rest

definitions.note: a description: what a reckless person does

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, its middle letters
toying with something means playing about with it, so the letters get moved around

blocks.note: the two middle letters of Ukip
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reckless messes with Ukip's core, and the rest is left to ask questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless person ignores danger, and so habitually chances things that might go wrong, behaving with daring.

clue.text: Boris's thing in front of the camera? Crew only embarrassed

definitions.text: Boris's thing in front of the camera

indicators.note: an embarrassed person is thrown into confusion, so the letters are thrown about too

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson's on-camera antics leave only the film crew red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson's public persona relies on comic buffoonery, so playing the fool on television is his trademark.

clue.text: Dicky in pain with sex (Paris finished him off)

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: an ache is a dull pain
dicky means unwell or unsound, as in a dicky heart
S, taken as a short form of sex

explanation.surface: Someone ill and sore is having sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' is not the city but the Trojan prince, whose arrow struck the Greek hero in the heel. Dicky is British slang for unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Trojan prince Paris killed the warrior hero with an arrow to his one vulnerable heel.

clue.text: see 24ac.
(& 29ac.) Sarah Palin politically? Traditionally, a real stirrer in the corridors of power etc.

definitions.text: Traditionally, a real stirrer in the corridors of power etc.

blocks.note: first meaning: a woman of the American ... Party movement

blocks.clueFragment: Traditionally, a real stirrer in the corridors of power etc.
blocks.note: second meaning: the woman who wheeled the ... trolley round offices, stirring cups

explanation.surface: Sarah Palin is painted as a political troublemaker stirring things up among the powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirrer' suggests a troublemaker, but she literally stirs the tea. A British tea lady served drinks from a trolley in offices.
explanation.definitionFit: Palin is a figurehead of the Tea Party right, and a female office worker who served hot drinks was known by this name.

clue.text: Boris becoming new leader probably Cameron's argument backing up faster reforms – Sam's initiative?

definitions.text: Boris becoming new leader probably Cameron's

indicators.note: backing up means moving backwards, so the word is written in reverse
to reform is to form again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
an initiative here is an initial, the first letter of the name

blocks.note: a row is a quarrel
taken as written
the first letter of Sam, Samantha Cameron

explanation.surface: Cameron dreads Boris taking over, with his wife Sam pushing reforms faster.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam is Samantha Cameron, the prime minister's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival's takeover is the outcome a party leader would dread most, the nightmare scenario.

clue.text: One to forcibly put down a tosspot

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who plonks, sets things down heavily
second meaning: a fool, in British slang

explanation.surface: A drunkard who needs to be firmly squashed.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonker is British slang for an idiot, made famous by the sitcom Only Fools and Horses; a tosspot is an insult too, originally a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: To plonk is to set something down heavily, and the noun is also a mild British insult for a stupid person.

clue.text: Ultra CV, i.e. dodgy as a top banker's job?

definitions.note: describes the job; the answer is the adjective for it

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and not straight, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, CV for curriculum vitae and i.e. as letters

explanation.surface: A senior banker's job demands an exceptional, possibly fudged, CV.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior bankers earn enormous salaries and bonuses, so their posts are highly profitable ones.

clue.text: Dissolute Cyclops: "head going for a song"

indicators.note: the head, the opening letter, leaves and the next word takes its place
dissolute means loose and wild in behaviour, so the letters are let loose

blocks.note: the setter's pseudonym, taken as written
taken as written; it replaces the leading C

explanation.surface: The setter, a debauched Cyclops, bursts into song with his head flung back.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a West Indian style of song, originally from Trinidad, with improvised topical lyrics.

clue.text: Bloody group underwear one has produces chafing

blocks.note: A is one of the blood groups
bras are items of women's underwear
I've, short for I have, with I as one

explanation.surface: Someone's underwear is causing a painful rub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a swear word but points to blood groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrasive scrapes or rubs roughly against a surface, which is exactly what chafing does to skin.

clue.text: China welcomed by Arabic militant leaders – ISIS, maybe?

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, here the opening letters of two words
being welcomed by someone means being taken in, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the first letters of Arabic and militant
china means mate, from rhyming slang china plate; a crony is a mate

explanation.surface: A militant group of Arabs takes in someone from China.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so china is a friend, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: ISIS stands for Islamic State of Iraq and Syria, a name formed from the initial letters of a longer title.

clue.text: Balls covered with honey (not hot, but energy-filled), Cyclops-style?

indicators.note: not tells you to leave out the letter for the following word
being filled means having something put inside, so a letter goes in

blocks.note: taken as written; in a down entry it covers, sits on top of, the next piece
Ed Balls, Labour's shadow chancellor at the time
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps; it is removed
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Testicles smeared with honey, in the manner of the one-eyed setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' is not testicles but the Labour politician Ed Balls; in a down entry, the honey covers him by sitting on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Cyclops had a single eye in the middle of his forehead, the setter's namesake.

clue.text: Far from broad head of prick, rather rough

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, the first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of prick
rude-ish, somewhat crude

explanation.surface: A crude remark about an uncouth bloke who is no good with women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broad' looks like a woman, but here it means coarse or risqué, as in broad humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad humour is coarse and bawdy, so someone easily shocked by such vulgarity is very far from it.

clue.text: Sound unit secured by celeb getting pissed with Di

clue.text: Crooked direct bank loan?

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bent bank making shady loans directly.

clue.text: Put coyly, the means by which you have the piss taken out of you

definitions.text: Put coyly, the means by which you have the piss taken out of you

blocks.clueFragment: the means by which you have the piss taken out of you
blocks.note: surface reading: whatever gets you mocked, since taking the piss is British slang for teasing
setter's reading: a polite euphemism for the body's urinary system, which literally removes urine

explanation.walkthrough: To take the piss is British slang for mocking someone; read literally, it describes the bladder at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a coy euphemism for the urinary organs, as a doctor might ask about them delicately.

clue.text: Labour leader engaged in off-target wit

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
being engaged in something means being caught up within it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a shot that is wide misses its target
the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: The Labour leader's attempts at jokes keep missing the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was the celebrated Irish playwright famed for epigrams, so he is the archetypal wit.

clue.text: (& 10ac.) Dodge Tory trap

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative
a trick catches someone out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodge' looks like a verb for avoiding the trap, but it is the noun meaning a swindle.

clue.text: Called in Cameron, a mediocrity

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the next two

clue.text: Heartless Dicky in seedy surroundings – a scene of innocent bliss

blocks.note: seedy can mean unwell
the first and last letters of Dicky

explanation.walkthrough: Seedy here means off-colour rather than sleazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a peaceful, picturesque scene or episode, typically pastoral and untroubled.

clue.text: Joint flop incurs attack from above

blocks.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club
a show that bombs is a failure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' is not a body part or a spliff but a cheap establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To dive-bomb is to swoop steeply down on a target from the air before releasing bombs.

clue.text: Idle bum needs stiff whip

to whip is to beat

explanation.surface: A lazy layabout deserves a good flogging.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadbeat is a lazy, aimless person who avoids work and responsibilities, a loafer.
